## 1️⃣ MISSING FIELDS IN useTablePersistence

### activeTab
- **What**: Tracks which tab user is viewing: `"open"` | `"close"`
- **Why**: OrganizationTrades has TWO separate tabs (Close-in trades vs Close-out trades)

## 2️⃣ SAVING MECHANISM: ARE THEY EQUAL?

### useViewPersistence (Manual Save)
```tsx
const saveToPersistence = debounce(() => {
  if (isFirstRender.current) return;
  saveTabState({
    columnFilters,
    columnVisibility,
    density,
    globalFilter,
    showGlobalFilter,
    showColumnFilters,
    sorting,
    columnOrder,
    columnSizing,
    columnPinning,
    grouping,
    filterType,        // ← Custom field
    startDate,         // ← Custom field
    endDate,           // ← Custom field
    selectedCommodity, // ← Custom field
    selectedBroker,    // ← Custom field
    selectedClearer,   // ← Custom field
    selectedBook,      // ← Custom field
  });
}, 500);  // ← DEBOUNCED 500ms

useEffect(() => {
  saveToPersistence();  // ← Called every render
}, [columnFilters, columnVisibility, ..., saveToPersistence]);
```

**Timeline:**
- State changes → useEffect fires → `saveToPersistence()` called
- If another change happens within 500ms → timer resets
- After 500ms of silence → actual save to localStorage

---

### useTablePersistence (Automatic Save)
```tsx
const [state, setState] = useState(() => {
  const saved = localStorage.getItem(storageKey);
  return saved ? JSON.parse(saved) : initialState;
});

const isInitialized = useRef(false);

useEffect(() => {
  if (!isInitialized.current) {
    isInitialized.current = true;  // ← Skip first render
    return;
  }
  
  localStorage.setItem(storageKey, JSON.stringify(state));
}, [state, storageKey]);  // ← Triggered on EVERY state change
```

**Timeline:**
- State changes → automatic `setState()` update
- useEffect hook fires immediately
- Saves to localStorage right away (no debounce)

| Scenario | useViewPersistence | useTablePersistence |

| User changes 10 filters in 2 seconds | **1 localStorage write** (debounced) | **10 localStorage writes** (immediate) |
| Performance | Better (fewer I/O ops) | Slower (more I/O ops) |
| Data freshness | Slightly delayed | Immediate |
